derived_results.claim: The frozen q sampler admits the exact independent transform R~Beta(31/2,3), U=(X+1)/2~Beta(37/2,37/2), W=4R/(1-R), y=2 sqrt(a) X/sqrt((1-R)(1-X^2)). Equal-CDF N-by-N bins therefore have exactly 1/N^2 mass and can replace product Gauss-Jacobi quadrature by a lower Riemann sum.

On each enlarged R/X box, W/y extrema plus the theta-cell geometry give a closed lower bound for H_mu. Negative boxes use the r92 global p_theta/p_rho<=3.817 ceiling; nonnegative boxes lower-bound p_min and upper-bound p_rho monotonically. This yields a deterministic mathematical L_cell lower envelope without W-tail truncation or a quadrature remainder theorem.

For N=128 and +/-1e-8 widened quantile brackets, the empirical worst theta cell has lower sum 10.243150288664415 in float64 and 10.243150288664445757661662665270647... in an independent 50-digit mpmath recomputation. All 127 interior quantiles on each axis were bracket-checked at 60 decimal digits; minimum CDF slack is 1.733e-9 on R and 2.927e-9 on U.

negative_or_scope_evidence: The proof reduction and equal-probability-cell logic are deterministic, but the beta-quantile brackets are high-precision mpmath checks rather than an independent directed-rounding incomplete-beta certificate.
The >10.24 lower sum is stable between float64 and 50-digit mpmath, but cell arithmetic has not yet been outward-rounded end-to-end.
Only the empirical worst theta cell is covered by the new partition certificate in this run; the next six low-margin cells remain.
The Decimal endpoint certificate is scoped to the frozen decimal constants of the standardized m=32 setup.
All results remain restricted to the clean standardized NIG/four-corner iid Gaussian problem.

candidate_new.mechanism: For heavy-tailed predictive integrals with a strong pointwise lower envelope, transform to independent bounded coordinates, partition each coordinate by exact probability quantiles, and lower-bound the integrand on widened boxes. Equal cell mass removes numerical integration weights, while analytic negative-branch ceilings prevent tail cancellation. This can be easier to machine-certify than high-order quadrature.
